text:
incident-bot: @oncall pager: elevated error rate and OOMs observed in inference pool 'dedicated-us-west-1-gpu-pool-3' related to KV cache allocator. Alerts: 5xx spike, CUDA OOMs, latency cliffs. Incident severity: P1.

maria: noticed a cluster-wide spike ~2m ago, tracing points to continuous-batching path. KV cache size jumped ~3x on several pods then allocator failures.

samir: pulling logs now. Which model?

maria: a mix but mostly 'redwood/llama-70b-8k-quant' serving long-chat sessions. High prefix reuse -> heavy KV cache growth.

jonah: @maria can you run `kubectl get pods -n redwood | grep kv` and paste pod names? I'll start isolating.

maria: pods: rwi-infer-3a-01, rwi-infer-3a-02, rwi-infer-3a-04. All three showing cuda OOM frenzy and frequent `cuda_malloc` retries. Logs: 

```
E CudaOutOfMemory: Failed to allocate 8.0 GiB (out of 12.0 GiB) at torch/cuda/allocator.cpp:...
KVCacheAllocator: arena fragmentation > 0.85, live_allocs=120k, free_segments=234
continuous-batcher: batch_size jumped from 8 -> 64 due to backlog
```

lina: interesting — continuous-batching allowed batch sizes to balloon because backlog of small requests with shared prefixes triggered aggressive batching heuristics. That increases KV cache requirements per request (longer seq * more entries).

support-rupert: Customer impact: two enterprise customers (Acme Health, BrightRetail) reported elevated latency and some 503s in last 10 mins. Support tickets are open.

maria: mitigation idea: temporarily cap batch size to 8 and reduce max_latency_ms to 50ms, and enable aggressive KV eviction TTL to force cache churn. We can push config via runtime flags to the serving runtime, should be low-risk.

samir: +1. Also there are known PyTorch/CUDA allocator fragmentation issues when many mid-sized allocations happen; quick workaround is to set `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:64` and restart the process to force different allocator arena behavior. That could reduce fragmentation.

jonah: can we avoid full restarts? Maybe tune the runtime's internal arena by calling `torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats()`? Not reliable. A rolling restart of the three affected pods is acceptable for now if we coordinate canary.

maria: proposing steps: 1) apply runtime config hotfix (cap continuous batching: max_batch=8, max_batch_timeout_ms=50), 2) set eviction TTL: kv_cache.eviction_ttl_ms=30000, 3) set env PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:64 on new pods, 4) canary restart rwi-infer-3a-01, monitor 1m, then roll.

ops-bot: deploy request created: hotfix/kv-cache-batch-cap. Canary target: rwi-infer-3a-01.

samir: I'll do the canary restart. @jonah can you update the support incident with ETA?

jonah: ETA canary 4m, full roll 20m if green. Updating support now.

support-rupert: noted. Triage note: Acme Health sees 4-8s tail latencies, BrightRetail sees intermittent 503. Both flagged as impacting user flows.

maria: starting canary patch: applying runtime flags via runtime-config API: 

```json
{"continuous_batching": {"max_batch_size": 8, "max_latency_ms": 50}, "kv_cache": {"eviction_ttl_ms": 30000}}
```

samir: canary restart done for rwi-infer-3a-01. New pod rwi-infer-3a-01-v2 up. env: PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:64.

maria: monitoring metrics: KV cache size on canary dropped ~60% after eviction TTL kicked in and batch cap prevented new blowups. No OOMs so far.

ops-bot: alert suppression: temporarily suppress repeated cuda_oom alerts for pods rwi-infer-3a-01/02/04 while rollout in progress.

samir: rolling to rwi-infer-3a-02 now.

lina: quick analysis: allocator fragmentation hit because many mid-sized tensors (~1-8MB) allocated for KV cache entries; default CUDA caching allocator uses large arenas leading to fragmentation under variable lifetimes. Reducing max_split_size_mb encourages splitting large allocations which in practice reduces contiguous fragmentation. We'll still need long-term changes.

maria: roll completed. Monitoring shows 503s dropped to near-zero, 95th latency back to baseline for canary then for cluster. No new OOMs in last 7 mins.

support-rupert: updated customers: Acme Health and BrightRetail were notified: mitigation applied, we're monitoring. They acknowledged and requested postmortem.

jonah: any other impacted services? Logging shows a couple of background batch jobs experienced elevated mem pressure but not OOM.

samir: adding additional safeguards: 1) guardrail in the runtime to prevent continuous-batcher from increasing batch size beyond X when per-request KV cache promises exceed Y, 2) metric `kv_cache.fragmentation_ratio` and `cuda_allocator.free_segments` added to dashboard, 3) alert rule to page on fragmentation_ratio > 0.7 plus sustained OOM rate.

lina: for long-term: evaluate switching allocator to use split arenas tuned for KV cache pattern, or implement a slab for KV entries (fixed-size blocks) to avoid fragmentation of many small mid-sized allocations. Also evaluate per-model TTL policies and per-session cache caps.

alice: creating a postmortem ticket and linking config diffs. I'll capture timeline: detection -> canary -> patch -> roll -> customer notif.

maria: timeline note: root cause appears to be interaction of continuous-batching heuristics and allocator fragmentation. Batching heuristics allowed large batch size growth under high prefix reuse (long KV vectors), which multiplied memory overhead and triggered fragmentation-driven OOMs in the CUDA allocator.

support-rupert: customers all set to be notified that we will follow up with a detailed postmortem and potential SLA credit if needed.

jonah: post-roll checks: 1) no OOM logs in 10m, 2) 95th latency within 10% of baseline, 3) customer checks passed. All good so far.

maria: closing pager in 10m if stable. Added follow-ups: - open RFC for allocator/specialized slab cache (eng-runtime) - add canary gating on KV cache growth - add a low-latency fallback path that disables continuous-batching for sessions flagged as high prefix reuse.

samir: one more data point: reproduced fragmentation in a local harness by simulating 10k sessions with varied seq lengths; confirmed `max_split_size_mb` tweak reduced fragmentation by ~45%. Will push reproducibility test to tests/frag-harness.

ops-bot: deploy hotfix/kv-cache-batch-cap: SUCCESS on 3/3 pods.

incident-bot: Pager resolved: no active on-call pages for this incident. Please file postmortem within 48h.

alice: filing postmortem: https://redwood/pmo/INC-1743456789 (placeholder). Assigning owners: maria (incident lead), samir (allocator root cause), lina (batching heuristics).

maria: final note: thanks team for quick response. We'll schedule a follow-up runbook update to include an emergency knob to force KV eviction and a prebuilt canary for allocator config changes. :thumbsup:

support-rupert: customers acknowledged, closing support tickets as mitigated.

jonah: handoff to next shift: if fragmentation ratio rises above 0.5, page eng-sre. Leaving detailed monitoring links in the ticket.

lina: will prototype slab cache design and spike cost/latency tradeoffs.

samir: logging the exact CLI used for future: `kubectl set env deployment/rwi-infer --env PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:64` and runtime-config changes as in the ticket.

maria: thread locking in 15m.

ops-bot: incident-bot scheduled follow-up reminder in 24h to check perf regressions and confirm postmortem posted.

maria: thanks all.
